Azerbaijan is preparing visas and residence permits for digital nomads

On September 24, the Parliamentary Committee on Economic Policy reviewed amendments to the Migration Code. If the law passes, starting from January 1, 2027, foreigners working remotely will be able to obtain a business visa, temporary residence permit, and even permanent residency. This is not for every freelancer with a laptop. The list is narrow: IT, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, innovations.

The income threshold is tied to the local minimum wage. Currently, it is 400 manats, around 235 dollars. To apply for a visa or temporary residence permit, one must demonstrate an average overseas income for the last six months not less than 13 times the minimum wage - 5,200 manats, approximately 3,060 dollars per month. For permanent residency, the threshold is doubled: 26 times the minimum wage, around 6,120 dollars.

The temporary residence permit is granted for up to three years with the possibility of extension. An invitation from the receiving party is not required. There is also no examination on the Azerbaijani language and basic legislation, which is the main privilege. Then, conditions begin that are not present in the usual "nomad visa for a year and then leave."

To obtain a residence permit or permanent residency, one will have to register for tax purposes and work as a resident of the technopark. Additionally, the individual becomes part of the state social insurance. This scheme is closer to that of a specialist whom the country wants to retain in its digital zone, rather than a tourist with Wi-Fi.

In comparison with the market, Thailand on DTV requires savings of around 500,000 baht and does not require a local tax on foreign income if you do not become a tax resident. Malaysia holds the threshold for tech professionals from 24,000 dollars per year. Azerbaijan sets a monthly income higher than many Asian programs but offers a three-year residence permit upfront and a path to permanent residency — if you are willing to enter the technopark.

The law has not been passed yet. This is a committee draft. It is not possible to submit an application now. It makes sense to follow the text until January: the wording "resident of the technopark" will determine whether this is a real entry point for remote workers or only a filter for those already treated as investors by Baku.

📌 Governance Quorum: Why a Vote Can Fail Even With a Majority

Main Points
⏺ Quorum is the minimum participation required for a decision to pass
⏺ Even if most voters choose “yes,” a proposal can fail without enough turnout
⏺ This post explains why DAOs need participation, not just votes

1️⃣ Core Idea — quorum protects a protocol from decisions made by a tiny group.
2️⃣ Example — if only a few wallets vote, the result may be technically “yes” but weakly representative.
3️⃣ Why It Matters — important changes should pass with meaningful participation from holders or delegates.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — quorum that is too high can freeze decisions, while quorum that is too low makes governance vulnerable.
5️⃣ Practical Check — when judging a DAO, review quorum rules, vote distribution, and delegate activity.

Final Thoughts

Governance is not only about who won. It also matters how many people showed up. Without quorum, a majority can be too small to count.

Here's a small fact about Python 🐍

The := operator is called the "walrus" because the symbols resemble the eyes and tusks of a walrus 🦭

It was introduced in Python 3.8 and allows you to assign a value to a variable and use it directly within the expression at the same time.

For example:

while (line := input("Say something: ")) != "quit":
    print(f"You said: {line}")

Without it, you would have to retrieve the value separately using input(), and then check it.

Have you ever used the := operator in your code?

The storm is producing persistent northeast winds (the reason it’s called a nor’easter), with gusts of 50–65 mph in the hardest-hit spots, especially along the coast from New Jersey through Long Island, Cape Cod, Martha’s Vineyard, and Nantucket. 

Rainfall totals of 2–6 inches (locally higher) are expected in many areas, and high tides are driving moderate to significant coastal flooding and beach erosion.  

New York and New Jersey have already declared states of emergency. Flights at the major NYC-area airports face disruptions, Amtrak service is at risk, and several big outdoor events have been canceled.  

Impacts through the weekend:  

Saturday into Sunday: 
Peak winds and heaviest rain for much of coastal southern New England and the mid-Atlantic.   
Lingering showers and gusty winds possible into Monday as the system slows and partially retrogrades. 
 
Stay safe out there folks, avoid unnecessary travel, watch for downed trees and power lines, and keep an eye on local forecasts and flood alerts.
